name: Isolated Small Intestine Duplication

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Enteric Duplication Cysts

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic or tubular structure with a well-developed smooth muscle wall contiguous with the native small intestine
Inner lining of the duplication cyst composed of gastrointestinal mucosa, often resembling small intestinal epithelium
Duplication cyst located isolated within the small intestine without associated anomalies of other gastrointestinal segments

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cystic structure with smooth muscle wall and gastrointestinal mucosal lining contiguous with small intestine
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by histopathological examination post-surgical resection or imaging combined with clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically detected in infants or young children

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intestinal obstruction due to cyst compression

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as expected

common.symptomName: Palpable abdominal mass on physical exam

occasional.symptomName: Gastrointestinal bleeding from ectopic gastric mucosa
searchTerms: gut bleeding from misplaced stomach tissue
intestinal bleeding from ectopic gastric lining
GI bleeding from abnormal stomach tissue

occasional.symptomName: Perforation of duplication cyst leading to peritonitis

rare.notes: Extremely rare but reported in adults

rare.symptomName: Fistula formation between duplication cyst and adjacent bowel
searchTerms: abnormal connection between cyst and bowel
systemic infection due to infected cyst

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers if cyst infected
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic lesion adjacent to small intestine with double wall sign
CT scan demonstrating well-defined cystic mass contiguous with small bowel
MRI delineating cyst morphology and relationship to adjacent bowel
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology confirming smooth muscle wall and gastrointestinal mucosal lining

distinguishingFeatures: Mesenteric cysts lack smooth muscle wall contiguous with intestine
True diverticulum arising from antimesenteric border of ileum
Communicates with intestinal lumen, unlike isolated cystic duplication

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain with peritonitis
references: Holcomb GW 3rd, Gheissari A, O'Neill JA Jr, Shorter NA, Bishop HC. Surgical management of alimentary tract duplications. Ann Surg. 1989 Jul;210(1):34-9.
Puligandla PS, Nguyen LT, St-Vil D, Flageole H, Bensoussan AL, Laberge JM. Gastrointestinal duplications. J Pediatr Surg. 2003 May;38(5):740-4.
